subject: Burst-window measurement and service-credit runbook — RFP appendix
messages:
From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@evercare-health.com>
To: marcus_lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: slo-rfp@evercare-health.com <slo-rfp@evercare-health.com>, procurement@evercare-health.com <procurement@evercare-health.com>
Date: Thu, 14 Aug 2025 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: RFP follow-up — measurement details for burst events and credit calc examples

Marcus — thanks for the initial RFP packet. We need a more prescriptive explanation of how Redwood measures partial outages that occur as short, high-intensity "burst" windows (e.g., 30s–5m spikes), how those are aggregated into daily uptime/latency metrics, and how service credits would be computed in multi-region, cross-probe scenarios.

Specifically:
- Which telemetry signals are authoritative for crediting (server-side probe pings, synthetic probes, real-customer traffic sampling)?
- How do you avoid double-counting the same degradation observed by multiple probes or regions?
- Please include a worked example (numbers) showing a multi-region incident where 1) a single shard has 3 short spikes, 2) a region-level probed outage, and 3) a cross-region latency degradation window — and what credit (if any) each scenario yields.

Can you send a short runbook + sample calculation spreadsheet we can attach to our procurement SOW? We may need this as an RFP appendix for our legal and SRE reviewers.

—Evelyn
Evelyn Hart
Senior Procurement Manager, EverCare Health

From: marcus.lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@evercare-health.com>
Cc: lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 14 Aug 2025 11:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RFP follow-up — measurement details for burst events and credit calc examples

Evelyn — thanks, this is exactly the sort of detail we want documented in the RFP appendix. Attached is a concise runbook (Redwood_SLO_Runbook_v1.3.pdf) and a sample calculator (sample_credit_calc_multiregion.xlsx) with three worked scenarios. Highlights:

- Authoritative telemetry: server-side token-level success/failure counts (primary), complemented by synthetic probe events (secondary) and sampled client-side telemetry (for corroboration). The runbook defines precedence: server telemetry > synthetic probes > client samples.

- Burst-window handling: we use a sliding-window aggregator with configurable windows (default 1m, 5m, 15m). Short spikes are assigned to the minimal window that captures the full degradation period; isolated sub-30s jitter is smoothed and excluded from credit triggering unless it contributes to an aggregate error-rate above the configured threshold (see section 4).

- Double-counting: each degradation is deduplicated by canonicalizing on request trace IDs and time-range overlap. If two probes observe the same underlying failed shard within a 60s overlap, we collapse to a single incident and attribute it to the shard/region with highest impact. The runbook includes the dedupe algorithm pseudo-steps.

- Crediting model: we compute a per-region impact fraction (fraction of total requests impacted per region), then normalize across regions to avoid >100% crediting. The spreadsheet contains the numeric examples you asked for (multi-shard, region-level outage, and cross-region latency scenario).

I'm looping Lauren (policy) and Neha (telemetry) to confirm wording for legal/SRE consumption. If helpful we can schedule a 30m workshop to walk through the calc sheet.

Attachments: Redwood_SLO_Runbook_v1.3.pdf, sample_credit_calc_multiregion.xlsx, probe_timing_diagram.png

Best,
Marcus Lin
Director, Platform Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
To: marcus.lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@evercare-health.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 15 Aug 2025 10:17:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RFP follow-up — measurement details for burst events and credit calc examples

Evelyn, Marcus — quick edits and clarifications:

- We should call out the legal boundary: credits are computed against the "billable token consumption" during the window, not against total potential capacity. Section 6.2 spells that out; suggest we add a one-paragraph legal summary at the top of the runbook for the SOW.

- Example numbers: I updated the calc sheet to show a multi-region example where Region A contributes 65% of impacted requests, Region B 25%, Region C 10%. For a 3-minute burst that crosses the 2% error threshold in Region A only, the final credit is computed as (impact_fraction_A * duration_weight) normalized by the customer's monthly uptime window (see tab "Calc_Example_3").

- Probe weighting: add a bullet that synthetic probes are weighted 0.6 for detection and server telemetry 1.0 as authoritative; client-side traces are only used for dispute resolution. That prevents synthetic-only anomalies from generating credits.

Marcus — can you confirm the exact threshold defaults we want in the runbook (error-rate %, sampling-reserve sizes) so we can include the precise numbers for the RFP? Neha, flagged to you for telemetry section confirmation.

Thanks — I recommend we send the updated package to EverCare with a short explanatory note and offer to do a walkthrough.

—Lauren Bishop
Senior Manager, Product Policy
Redwood Inference

From: neha_kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@evercare-health.com>, lauren_bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, marcus.lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 17 Aug 2025 15:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RFP follow-up — measurement details for burst events and credit calc examples

Evelyn — attaching the finalized runbook and sample calculators per Lauren's edits. I've set the default thresholds in section 4.1: error-rate trigger = 2.0% sustained over the 1-minute window OR 1.2% over a 5-minute rolling average; sampling reserve = 0.5% of total traffic for corroborative client traces (preserves privacy knobs). Probe weighting: server telemetry 1.0, synthetic probes 0.6, client samples 0.4 (only for dispute scenarios).

Worked examples included in the spreadsheet:
- Example A: three short shard spikes (45s total across two shards) -> no credit if aggregate weighted impact < 0.5% of monthly billable tokens.
- Example B: region-level probe outage of 4m -> credit computed as region_impact_fraction * outage_minutes normalized to 30-day window (spreadsheet shows numeric).
- Example C: cross-region latency degradation where all regions saw elevated p95 but only Region B crossed the severity threshold -> partial credit proportional to region impact fraction after deduplication.

Next steps: Marcus will upload the package to the EverCare Drive folder and I can apply document watermarks for distribution. Lauren — will you approve the one-paragraph legal summary so I can insert it as the runbook preface?

Evelyn — if this looks good I propose we supply the attachments and offer a 30-minute technical walkthrough. If EverCare prefers a different set of measurement thresholds for the agreement, we can show sensitivity tables that map thresholds to credit multipliers.

Regards,
Neha Kapoor
Principle Reliability Engineer, Observability
